title: The CEO Who Sold Stock in His Own Funeral
hook: He announced his own death, tanked the stock, bought it back, and then 'resurrected' as a billionaire.
why_this_can_go_viral: Combines death, deception, and massive wealth—three viral triggers in one hook.

title: The Supplier That Sold 'Human Hair' Wigs—Made from Prisoners Without Consent
hook: It wasn't donated hair. It was harvested from unconscious inmates in a state-run labor program.
why_this_can_go_viral: Shocking violation of bodily autonomy that most people never think about when buying beauty products.

title: The Startup That Sold 'Lifetime' Subscriptions—Then Declared Bankruptcy to Escape Them
hook: They promised forever access, collected millions, then legally 'died' to reset their liabilities.
why_this_can_go_viral: Relatable anger—everyone hates losing access to something they paid for forever.

title: The Monopoly That Bought All the Funeral Homes—Then Raised the Price of Dying
hook: One company now controls 20% of US funerals. They made grief a subscription service.
why_this_can_go_viral: Death is universal; revealing that someone profits from it unfairly triggers deep indignation.

title: The Spy Who Became a Competitor's Janitor—and Found Their Patent in the Trash
hook: He swept floors for two years, waiting for one engineer to throw away a crumpled blueprint.
why_this_can_go_viral: The lowly janitor archetype subverts expectations—viewers love the undercover angle.

title: The Ad That Made You Believe Washing Machines Were Killing Your Family
hook: They sold a 'disinfectant' by making you terrified of your own laundry. Then it turned out the germs were fake.
why_this_can_go_viral: Exposes how companies create problems to sell solutions—a classic dark marketing reveal.

title: The Hedge Fund That Bought a Weather Station—to Predict Crop Failures Before Farmers
hook: They owned the data, let farmers starve, then shorted the grain futures.
why_this_can_go_viral: Combines weather, food, and Wall Street greed—a perfect storm of outrage and curiosity.

title: The Company That Sold 'Cancer Insurance'—Then Denied Everyone Who Got Cancer
hook: They defined 'cancer' so narrowly that stage-4 patients were told they had a 'benign growth.'
why_this_can_go_viral: Exploits a universal fear—getting sick—and reveals the legalized cruelty behind insurance contracts.

title: The Founder Who Paid People to Post Fake Rave Reviews—Then Sued Them for Libel
hook: He hired actors to praise his product, then when competitors did the same, he sued them into bankruptcy.
why_this_can_go_viral: Reveals a hidden legal weapon—weaponized fake reviews—that most people don't know exists.

title: The Oil Company That Secretly Bought the Government's Seismic Data—to Find Oil Before They Did
hook: They knew exactly where to drill before the land was even auctioned. That data was supposed to be public.
why_this_can_go_viral: Feels like a heist movie—stealing geological secrets from the government itself.

title: The Sugar Company That Paid Dentists to Say 'Cavities Are Genetic'
hook: They funded entire dental school curriculums to teach that brushing didn't matter—only fluoride did.
why_this_can_go_viral: Attacks a universally accepted belief—that sugar causes cavities—and flips it into a corporate conspiracy.

title: The Supplier That Sold 'Virgin Olive Oil' That Was Actually Lamp Oil with Green Dye
hook: It wasn't food. It was industrial lubricant, repackaged and sold on the same shelf as real olive oil.
why_this_can_go_viral: Visually shocking—people pour 'olive oil' on salads that was never meant for human consumption.

title: The CEO Who Sold 'Eco-Friendly' Packaging—That Was Made from Toxic Sludge
hook: It was branded green, certified compostable, and loaded with heavy metals that leached into soil.
why_this_can_go_viral: Environmental hypocrisy is a massive trigger—people hate being duped by 'green' labels.

title: The Monopoly That Owns the Only Railroad—and Uses It to Starve Towns That Refuse to Pay Up
hook: They blocked grain shipments, stopped coal deliveries, and watched a town freeze—just to win a rate dispute.
why_this_can_go_viral: Gives monopoly a human face—literal starvation as a negotiation tactic is pure dark drama.

title: The Trader Who Faked a CEO's Heart Attack—with a Single Phone Call to a Nurse
hook: He called the hospital posing as a relative, got the CEO's condition changed to 'critical,' and the stock tanked instantly.
why_this_can_go_viral: Incredible audacity and simplicity—a single phone call made millions. Viewers will replay it in disbelief.

title: The Bank That Financed a Mine—Then Foreclosed on the Town's Water Rights
hook: They lent the mine money, it failed, and they took the town's entire aquifer as collateral.
why_this_can_go_viral: Water scarcity is a looming global crisis—showing a bank profiting from it is enraging and shareable.

title: The Spy Who Used a Competitor's Own Delivery Truck to Steal Their Client List
hook: He bribed one driver, replaced the manifest, and the entire route of clients got poached in 48 hours.
why_this_can_go_viral: Low-tech, high-impact—viewers love simple but effective heists they could imagine pulling off.

title: The Ad That Used Subliminal 'Death' Images to Make You Buy Cigarettes
hook: They flashed skulls for 1/24th of a second. It didn't scare you—it made you crave smoke.
why_this_can_go_viral: Subliminal anything is inherently fascinating—adding death and addiction makes it irresistible.

title: The Toy Company That Sold Dolls That 'Learned' Your Child's Voice—Then Shared It with Advertisers
hook: The doll listened to everything. Your child's secrets were sold to the highest bidder before bedtime.
why_this_can_go_viral: Children's safety is an emotional nuclear button—combining toys, AI, and data theft is explosive.

title: The Startup That Sold 'Free' Shipping—Then Shipped Everything by the Slowest Possible Method
hook: They made billions on 'free shipping' by routing packages through Antarctica to delay delivery by months.
why_this_can_go_viral: Absurd and relatable—everyone has waited forever for a package, and this reveals the 'why.'

title: The Chemical Company That Dumped Waste into a Volcano—and Called It 'Disposal Innovation'
hook: They claimed it would 'neutralize' underground. Instead, it poisoned the entire island's water table.
why_this_can_go_viral: Volcanoes are visually stunning—using one as a trash can is a jaw-dropping concept.

title: The Supplier That Sold 'Gold' Bars That Were Actually Tungsten Painted Yellow
hook: They floated on the world market for years, fooling banks, refineries, and even X-ray scanners.
why_this_can_go_viral: Gold is the ultimate symbol of value—faking it at industrial scale is a modern alchemy story.

title: The CEO Who Hired Actors to Be 'Employees' in the Office—to Hide a Mass Layoff
hook: Visitors saw a bustling office. In reality, 90% of the desks were occupied by paid extras.
why_this_can_go_viral: Theater-of-the-absurd meets corporate fraud—visual of empty desks with paid actors is unforgettable.

title: The Bank That Charged You $35 for a 'Negative Balance'—When You Had $5,000 in Savings
hook: They counted your checking and savings as separate companies, so you were 'overdrawn' while sitting on cash.
why_this_can_go_viral: Nearly everyone has been hit by an overdraft fee—revealing the deliberate design behind it is infuriating.
